releaseNotes: check:secrets had a dead exemption and has been warning about the one document whose job is to explain credential handling. The credential-extraction scan skips the skill's own guidance prose, and it identified that prose by directory name: `references/`. That directory became `playbook/` in v0.53.0 and this line was never renamed with it, so for eight releases the exemption matched nothing and playbook/operations/secrets-management.md was reported as if it were an app repo leaking a key. A path segment that stops matching does not error, it just quietly stops exempting, which is the same failure family as v0.61.1's unanchored regex: the gate fails the documents it exists to protect, and the only escape routes are editing shared tooling or doctoring the document.

The exemption now names playbook/, and two fixtures pin it so the next rename cannot repeat this silently. One proves the skill's own playbook prose may show an extraction snippet without warning; the other proves an app-side references/ directory is still scanned. The second matters more than it looks: renaming without it would leave a security gate that any repo could silence by naming a folder references/. Both assert the specific issue code rather than an exit status, because this scan emits a warning and warnings do not change the exit code, so a fixture asserting only exit 0 would pass whether or not the warning fired.

107 unused declarations are gone and the compiler now rejects new ones. Splitting the fixture suite into modules in v0.55.0 and v0.56.0 gave every module the full shared helper import list while each uses only a subset, leaving 103 dead imports across five fixture files plus four in gates/. Two of the four were computed values that looked like bugs and were not: check-app-copy.ts built both a Set and an array of allowed terms and scrubbed using only the array, so the exemptions were honoured and the Sets were merely redundant. tsc is the oracle for all 107 — it reported zero reads before removal and stays clean after. noUnusedLocals is now set in both tsconfig.json files and was verified to fire on a planted dead local, so the class cannot come back. noUnusedParameters was left off deliberately: it currently reports zero, and enabling a rule with nothing to catch trades real friction on callback signatures for no present gain.

Sixteen commands in AGENTS.md pointed at skill/b2c-mobile-business-launch/templates, a directory renamed to business/ in v0.54.0. They did not fail loudly. Each resolved against a path that does not exist and printed fabricated errors — PROJECT_STATE.yaml is missing, BUSINESS_ACCESS.md is missing — so a maintainer sanity-checking the repo from the canonical maintainer guide got a plausible-looking failure report about nothing. All sixteen now point at business/ and were run to confirm they execute against the real fixtures and report zero errors.

README.md and ARCHITECTURE.md now describe the tree that exists. The README's repo layout omitted gates/ entirely — 58 validators, the largest directory in the skill — while still crediting scripts/ with holding validators and listing evals/ as top-level when it has been machine/evals/ since v0.56.0; spine.md had been missing since v0.58.0. ARCHITECTURE.md claimed every top-level directory answers who reads it while never mentioning agents/, design-system/ or render/, so a reader trusting that claim as an inventory would miss three shipped directories. A paragraph now covers them as shipped payload rather than audience-sorted content, and records that the root design-room.html is a real static render of the skill's own state rather than a stale twin of the one under business/ — their design-state hashes differ because they render different state.

The business/docs and business/pages sub-split is now recorded as deferred rather than pending, with the reason attached. v0.61.0 froze the eight page filenames at the root of business/ when it made four of them generated, and check:generated-pages reads that root non-recursively. Four are evidence paths in PROJECT_STATE.yaml and the set carries roughly 194 references repo-wide, so the sub-split is a rewrite of that whole reference surface in exchange for grouping alone. Left unmarked it reads as forgotten work; the entry now says what it costs and when to take it.

Two finished work prompts moved from docs/brainstorms/ to docs/history/, and the convention that sends them there is now written in AGENTS.md instead of living only inside one file's justification of its own placement. The simplification prompt asserted that main was at v0.60.0 and that generated pages were open work, and it shipped in the very commit that closed them, so it was false on arrival. A finished prompt left where ideas are still being weighed is worse than a deleted one: the next session greps for open work, finds a confident step list, and redoes it. Both now carry a banner saying what they described, when, and what has since shipped, and both are kept for their reasoning — the trap lists inside them are why later refactors stopped rediscovering the same failures.
